Internal certification and a complete task card are not external scientific validation.

tasks.certification_reason: Active rate-law identification: the candidate spends a 28-call budget on a substrate-and-inhibitor assay, names one of six published laws with its constants, and declines on the three worlds that obey none. Competitive, uncompetitive and noncompetitive inhibition are provably inseparable from a single substrate titration, so the score turns on designing the experiment rather than on recalling the laws. One out-of-family world is a cooperative enzyme that is also competitively inhibited: at zero inhibitor it fits Hill to 0.9 sigma, so a candidate that does not vary the inhibitor books a false discovery rather than merely scoring low. Ablating the reference measures what each competence is worth - 0.990 with three inhibitor levels and both refusal tests, 0.315 with one level, 0.490 when never declining, 0.000 with neither - and blanket abstention scores 0.000 by construction. A Claude Opus 5 draw on 2026-09-02 settles it: three seeds, first proposal 0.9905 / 0.9882 / 0.9890 against the reference's 0.9904, law identification 1.00, false discovery 0.00, 28 of 28 assay calls. The winning program titrates at three inhibitor levels and runs both refusal tests; there is no exploit in it. Saturated for the current frontier and retained as an on-ramp that still separates a naive analysis from a competent one, not as frontier evidence. The draw also moved a public key: the model wrote float() on noise_sigma_hint, which held a sentence, and nine of nine proposals scored zero on the naming before the fix.

Ablation: 0.730 with decomposition, replication and regression; 0.006 with grid-midpoint boundaries; 0.444 never declining; 0.000 for the naive grid, with a 0.86 false-phase rate. The reference deliberately sits at 0.730 on half the budget, so the boundary axis retains headroom; the admission bar recorded on the card is that a first Opus 5 proposal must not reach it - and a Claude Opus 5 draw on 2026-09-02 (clean-revision run) passed: first proposals 0.10 / 0.67 / 0.34 against the reference's 0.730, best of nine 0.6706, none reaching the reference. Unsaturated at the frontier; the run is single-arm at budget 3, so it shows headroom, not yet feedback-driven improvement.

Evidence synthesis migrated out of clinical trials: eight groups publish a value and a one-sigma uncertainty for the same constant and scatter further than those uncertainties allow. Four defects are possible - sound, globally understated errors, one group with an unquoted systematic, or two methods that disagree - and the three defective ones overlap in chi-square per degree of freedom (2.2-11.8, 1.8-5.7, 3.9-10.2 against a sound table's 0.4-1.9), so the diagnosis is not reachable from the published table. It is reachable from five charged split tests against eight groups, and only by spending them at both ends of the deviation ordering: the deviant tail splits badly under both a single systematic and a global understatement, so the tail alone halves culprit identification. Ablation - 0.842 buying at both ends, 0.701 on the deviant tail only, 0.586 on typical groups only, 0.425 buying nothing, 0.509 never declining, 0.000 declining everything. A Claude Opus 5 draw on 2026-09-02 reached the reference's 0.8421 on two of three seeds - one on the first proposal, one on the second after 0.6817 - and exceeded it on none. The third seed stalls at 0.6817 across all three proposals while buying 3.8 of its 5 split tests, which is the failure the axes exist to make legible. A harder on-ramp than EnzymeKineticsLaw and one that shows a real proposal-to-proposal gain, but the reference sits at the ceiling this scoring admits, so it is not frontier evidence.

Retained as a candidate pending external review, independent recomputation, and any model measurement.
